title: MZ Help porting MOG_CharPoses into MZ

posts.author: AmeerAshourDraws
posts.body:
Hey everyone, I currently need some help with the MOG_CharPoses plugin. For those unaware, this is an MV plugin made by MogHunter, who also made the Chrono Engine, which allowed characters to have different animations during certain states. I've been working on a project called the Schala Z System which is a port of the Chrono Engine to MZ, particularly Chrono Mode (I have on interest in ABS mode).
I've been porting a lot of other MOG plugins alongside it to make sure they work with the system, but now I'm currently stumped with the CharPoses plugin. Anytime I tried to use it after renaming the files appropriately, I would get this. I tried it on an empty project to double check if the Schala Z System was doing something wrong, but no, the same result happens.
I figured it could be because it's taking the Actor 1's dashing sprite and treating it like a giant one, you know the one where it has multiple actors grouped into one, but get this, whenever I try putting the $ sign to make it read it as a single character sprite sheet, it errors out completely. And whenever I set the actor to the character those sheets are based on, whether I added the $ or not, it would still crash and say it failed "%24Actor1_dash.png", even when adding the %24 part.
I have no clue what the problem could be other than MZ having a different method of rendering and managing sprite sheets than MV, in which I don't know exactly where to look since I'm still somewhat an amateur when it comes to JavaScript in RPG Maker. If anyone knows any answers or hints, do let me know

posts.author: AmeerAshourDraws
posts.body:
Okay, I tried screwing around a little with the scripts and also the Chrono Engine directly ported to MZ, and I think I found the culprit, which is not something I expected. Whenever I try the plugin in the ported Chrono Engine regardless if I have Fossil on or off, it works just fine. However, this is because it's still an MV project and that it's running off of MV's corescript. If at any point you update the corescript to any of MZ's versions (which is the case by default with all of my tests in blank MZ projects), the plugin will break entirely. I confirmed that by making a duplicate of the ported Chrono Engine and updated the corescript from "Unknown" (definitely MV's) to 1.9.0, and the entire project would barely boot up, even when I was using Fossil (which I just learned it was updated recently).
So, my solution here is to rewrite the plugin's syntax and code to make it work with MZ's corescript, which is gonna be tricky.

Okay... believe it or not, I managed to get it to work, and it is a quirk I noticed with the plugin. Basically, the issue was the fact that the base MZ characters that I was using were part of MZ's default Actors sheet, those are one of the big sprite sheets that have 8 sprite sheets in one. Turns out, if you have one of them selected for your character(s), the plugin then starts considering the other states as part of a big sprite sheet and only goes for what it thinks is the first sprite sheet.
The only way I fixed it was to make sure I selected the standard ones that had a $ at the start. This never happened to me before when I was testing the battles with the Schala Z System, but I guess that makes sense now that I know what's happening. I still don't know why the battles wouldn't activate, though, probably screwed something up in my end
